blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-ops-1 (Unbounded retry of a non-idempotent charge) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-ops-2 (Payment call has no timeout) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-ops-3 (Charge failures are swallowed without a log) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: Bound the retries (a few attempts) with exponential backoff, and retry only failures that are safe to repeat: send an idempotency key derived from order_id so the provider deduplicates a repeated charge, and do not retry 4xx responses. When the provider accepts a charge but the response is lost (connection reset, read error, 5xx after processing), the loop POSTs again every second and charges the customer twice; a definitive 4xx (card declined, invalid amount) is retried forever at a fixed 1 s, holding the checkout request and hammering the provider. After the last attempt, raise an error naming the order_id and the provider status.
findings.title: Unbounded retry of a non-idempotent charge

findings.recommendation: Pass timeout= (connect and read) to requests.post. Without it, a provider that accepts the connection but never answers blocks the checkout call forever; no RequestException is raised, so even the retry loop never runs, and the operator sees hung workers with nothing in the logs.
findings.title: Payment call has no timeout

findings.recommendation: Log each failed attempt as structured fields (order_id, attempt, HTTP status or exception type, never the card or credentials) and raise an actionable error when retries are exhausted. Today, when the provider is down or rejects the charge, the exception is dropped and the loop spins silently: an operator at 3 a.m. sees stalled checkouts and no error, metric or log line pointing at the payment provider.
findings.title: Charge failures are swallowed without a log

findings.recommendation: Read the provider URL from the environment or configuration. The endpoint differs between environments (sandbox vs. production): as written, every environment — tests and staging included — charges against the production endpoint, and switching it requires a new release.
findings.title: Provider URL hard-coded
